Bill number: HB1130
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 341
 By Lowe

 HOUSE BILL 1130

 By Farmer

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to school counselors.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 3, Part 1, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a)

 (1) Subject to appropriation, the department shall allocate to each LEA

 sufficient funds for the LEA to employ one (1) full-time licensed professional

 school counselor position at each high school in the LEA that enrolls at least six

 hundred (600) students in grades ten through twelve (10-12).

 (2) If an LEA employs one (1) or more part-time licensed professional

 school counselors at a high school that enrolls at least six hundred (600)

 students in grades ten through twelve (10-12), then the LEA may use any funds

 received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to employ the part-time licensed

 professional school counselor on a full-time basis. An LEA that converts a part-

 time licensed professional school counselor position to a full-time position

 pursuant to this subdivision (a)(2) satisfies the requirement in subsection (b).

 (3) If an LEA employs one (1) full-time licensed professional school

 counselor for every two hundred fifty (250) student members of the LEA, then the

 LEA may use any funds received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to supplant the

 cost to the LEA of employing the number of full-time licensed professional school

 counselors required to meet the specified ratio.

 (b) Each LEA shall employ one (1) full-time licensed professional school

counselor at each high school for which the LEA receives funding pursuant to this

section. This subsection (b) does not require an LEA that employs one (1) full-time

licensed professional school counselor position for every two hundred fifty (250) student

members of the LEA to employ any additional full-time licensed professional school

counselor positions beyond the number required for the LEA to meet the specified ratio.

 (c) The funds allocated to an LEA pursuant to this section are in addition to the

funds allocated to the LEA for purposes of the TISA.

 (d)

 (1) The state board may promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the roles and responsibilities required of a full-time

 licensed professional school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this

 section that exceed those required of school counselors in § 49-6-303.

 (2) The state board shall promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the amount of time each full-time licensed professional

 school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this section must dedicate

 to providing high school students the preventative and developmental counseling

 services required in § 49-6-303(b), one (1) or more of the counseling and

 guidance services listed in § 49-5-302(b), and any of the services required to

 comply with any additional roles and responsibilities established by the state

 board pursuant to subdivision (d)(1); provided, that each full-time licensed

 professional school counselor must dedicate at least seventy percent (70%) of

 the counselor's time to working directly with high school students.

 SECTION 2. This act is not an appropriation of funds, and funds shall not be obligated

or expended pursuant to this act unless the funds are specifically appropriated by the general

assembly.

 SECTION 3. For purposes of promulgating rules, this act takes effect upon becoming a

law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, this act takes effect July 1, 2025, the

public welfare requiring it, and applies to the 2025-2026 school year and each school year

thereafter.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would, if the General Assembly specifically appropriates funds, require the department to provide each LEA enough additional funding for one full-time licensed professional school counselor position at each high school with at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12. An LEA receiving the funding would have to employ a full-time counselor at each funded school. It could use the money to make an existing part-time counselor full-time. An LEA that already employs one full-time licensed professional school counselor for every 250 student members could instead use the money to cover its existing counselor costs and would not have to add positions beyond that ratio. The funding would be in addition to funds allocated for TISA.

The state board, in consultation with the department, could set additional duties for counselors in positions funded by the bill. It would have to set how much time those counselors spend on the specified counseling and guidance services and any additional duties. Each counselor would have to spend at least 70% of their time working directly with high school students. The bill would take effect upon becoming law for rulemaking. Its other provisions would take effect July 1, 2025, and apply beginning with the 2025–2026 school year.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would, if the General Assembly specifically appropriates funds, require the department to provide each LEA enough additional funding for one full-time licensed professional school counselor position at each high school with at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the appropriation condition, allocating agency, recipients, counselor qualifications, and school enrollment threshold.

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA receiving the funding would have to employ a full-time counselor at each funded school. It could use the money to make an existing part-time counselor full-time.
assessments.rationale: In the context of the previously defined eligible schools and counselors, identifies conversion as an allowed way to fulfill the employment requirement.

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA that already employs one full-time licensed professional school counselor for every 250 student members could instead use the money to cover its existing counselor costs and would not have to add positions beyond that ratio.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the qualifying staffing ratio and permission to replace local spending on the counselors employed to meet it.

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA receiving the funding would have to employ a full-time counselor at each funded school. It could use the money to make an existing part-time counselor full-time. An LEA that already employs one full-time licensed professional school counselor for every 250 student members could instead use the money to cover its existing counselor costs and would not have to add positions beyond that ratio.
assessments.rationale: Covers the employment requirement for funded schools and the exception for LEAs meeting the 1:250 ratio; counselor qualifications are established in the preceding sentence.

assessments.summary_quote: The funding would be in addition to funds allocated for TISA.
assessments.rationale: Expressly states that the funding supplements TISA allocations.

assessments.summary_quote: The state board, in consultation with the department, could set additional duties for counselors in positions funded by the bill.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the board's discretionary authority, required consultation, funded-position scope, and authority to establish duties beyond existing requirements.

assessments.summary_quote: The state board, in consultation with the department, could set additional duties for counselors in positions funded by the bill. It would have to set how much time those counselors spend on the specified counseling and guidance services and any additional duties. Each counselor would have to spend at least 70% of their time working directly with high school students.
assessments.rationale: Covers mandatory time allocation and the 70% direct-service minimum, but does not identify the preventative and developmental services or the requirement to include one or more of the separately listed counseling and guidance services.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would take effect upon becoming law for rulemaking.
assessments.rationale: States the immediate effective date for rulemaking purposes.

assessments.summary_quote: Its other provisions would take effect July 1, 2025, and apply beginning with the 2025–2026 school year.
